literal: Even the vast ocean its own abundance will diminish, if the cloud, having condensed, itself without giving becomes.
translation: Even the vast ocean's own abundance will diminish, if the cloud, having drawn its water, fails to give it back as rain.
modern: மேகமானது கடலிலிருந்து நீரை முகந்து கொண்டு சென்று, மீண்டும் மழையாகப் பொழியாமல் போனால், பரந்த கடலும் தன் வளம் குன்றிப் போகும்.
explanation: This couplet beautifully illustrates the water cycle and the concept of mutual dependence in nature. The word 'நீர்மை' refers to the ocean's inherent quality of abundance, wealth, and life-supporting nature. The poet explains that even the immense ocean, which seems to have an inexhaustible supply of water, will lose its richness and shrink if the clouds ('எழிலி') do not return the water they took. It teaches us that no matter how vast one's resources are, they will eventually deplete without the cycle of giving and receiving.
